newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu says met Arafat but Hebron deal elusive.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu says met Arafat but Hebron deal elusive.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said that he had met Palestinian President Yasser Arafat secretly on Sunday but they failed to clinch a deal on Hebron.

"I met with Yasser Arafat at the Erez Junction. I had hoped the meeting would remain a secret because I thought that would help build confidence," Netanyahu told businessmen in Tel Aviv. "We reached progress in certain areas but there are still issues that are in dispute."
"We are making progress but we still haven't reached full agreement on all the issues," he said.
"I want to tell you that I am optimistic in our ability to reach peace and security...and I have the patience required in such negotiations."

Netanyahu and Arafat have been trying to hammer out a deal to give Palestinians self-rule in the volatile West Bank town of 100,000 Arabs and 400 Jews. Security issues and other concerns have delayed the handover for 10 months.

U.S. Middle East envoy Dennis Ross took part in the meeting which lasted about four hours at the Israeli-Gaza border under the cover of darkness, officials said. News of the meeting leaked out hours later.
